title: Extended Cech complex and Koszul dual limit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ be global sections, allowing $r=0$. Use the module sheaves and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $P_m=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[0,r]$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with forward map $P_m\to P_{m+1}$ given in each factor by identity in degree zero and multiplication by $b_j$ in degree one. Equivalently the summand indexed by a subset $I$ in degree $|I|$ has transition multiplication by $\prod_{i\in I}b_i$. Its dual $Q_m=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,\mathcal O)$, after the usual dual-complex sign identification, is the tensor of the factors $[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ with inverse maps $(b_j,1)$. Let $C_b$ be the extended alternating complex with degree-zero term $\mathcal O$, degree-$q$ term $\prod_{|I|=q}\mathcal O[1/\prod_{i\in I}b_i]$, alternating localization differential, and augmentation $\epsilon:C_b\to\mathcal O[0]$ equal to identity in degree zero. Localization means sheafified sectionwise localization. There is an augmentation-compatible identification $C_b\cong\operatorname{colim}_m P_m$, and this degreewise filtered colimit represents the homotopy colimit in $D(\mathcal O)$. For every $N\in D(\mathcal O)$, represented by a complex $N^\bullet$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\theta_N:R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(C_b,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_m\operatorname{Tot}(N^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q_m).$$
Here derived internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; the tower on the right is a strict tower of complexes, each term represents $N\otimes^L Q_m$, and $R\lim$ is the total derived inverse limit computed with a K-injective strict-tower resolution, as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The isomorphism is independent of the representative of $N$ under the derived comparison maps. It carries $N\cong R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O,N)\xrightarrow{\epsilon^*}R\mathcal Hom(C_b,N)$ to the strict-tower unit induced by the degree-zero maps $\mathcal O\to Q_m$. For every object $U$, restriction of this comparison identifies its target with the corresponding strict derived limit on $\mathcal C/U$, and the comparisons commute with further slice restrictions and with morphisms in $N$. For the empty list $C_b=P_m=Q_m=\mathcal O[0]$ and the comparison and unit are the identity under the constant-tower identification.

proof.text: Expand $P_m$: its degree-$q$ summands have bases $e_I$ for $|I|=q$, and $d(e_I)=\sum_{j\notin I}(-1)^{|\{i\in I:i<j\}|}b_j^m e_{I\cup\{j\}}$. Put $t_I=\prod_{i\in I}b_i$. The identity $t_{I\cup\{j\}}b_j^m=t_I b_j^{m+1}$ verifies the forward maps are chain maps. In the dual Hom differential, the one-factor differential is $b_j^m$ from degree $-1$ to degree $0$; the transition is $(b_j,1)$. For the multi-factor dual, evaluate $\phi_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\phi_r$ on $p_1\otimes\cdots\otimes p_r$ with sign $(-1)^{\sum_{a<b}|\phi_b||p_a|}$, moving each $\phi_b$ past the earlier $p_a$. Substitution into $d\phi=-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi d_P$ gives the tensor dual differential, and degree-zero transition maps introduce no extra signs. Evaluation gives $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,N)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes Q_m)$: on homogeneous $x\in N^a$, $\phi\in Q_m^c$, send $x\otimes\phi$ to $(p\mapsto\phi(p)x)$ for $p\in P_m^{-c}$. Inserting the Hom differential gives $d_Nx\otimes\phi+(-1)^a x\otimes d_Q\phi$, and precomposition by $P_m\to P_{m+1}$ becomes $1_N\otimes(Q_{m+1}\to Q_m)$.

proof.text: For $I$, send $a e_I$ at stage $m$ to $a/t_I^m$. This is compatible with transition multiplication by $t_I$. Every fraction is represented at a sufficiently large stage; $a/t_I^m=a'/t_I^{m'}$ means a power of $t_I$ kills the cross-multiplied difference, exactly equality at a later stage. Perform this calculation on sections and sheafify, as required for the colimit of module sheaves. The insertion term $b_j^m a e_{I\cup\{j\}}$ maps to $a/t_I^m$ localized at $b_j$, with the alternating sign from step 1. Thus both differentials and the degree-zero projection agree with $C_b$ and $\epsilon$. For $I=\varnothing$, $t_I=1$ and this is the constant copy of $\mathcal O$.

Let $S=\bigoplus_m P_m$ and let $u:S\to S$ be identity minus the map sending the $m$-th summand to the $(m+1)$-st by its transition. The cited telescope theorem gives a canonical quasi-isomorphism $T=\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to C_b$. Hence $R\mathcal Hom(C_b,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(T,N)$ is an isomorphism. Choose the functorial K-injective resolution $N\to I$ supplied by the derived internal Hom definition, so the latter object is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(T,I)$.

Put $H_m=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,I)=\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes Q_m)$ with the strict inverse transitions from step 1. Every $H_m$ is K-injective by the bounded split-projective tensor theorem (each term of $Q_m$ is finite free). Set $B=\prod_m H_m$ termwise. The product-K-injective theorem identifies $B$ with the product in $D(\mathcal O)$, without assuming exact products of sheaves. The sheaf Hom universal property gives $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(S,I)=B$; precomposition by $u$ is $1-s$, where $(s h)_m=h_{m+1}\circ(P_m\to P_{m+1})$. Expanding the two summands of the mapping cone and its Hom differential identifies $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(T,I)$ with the mapping fibre $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:B\to B)[-1]$, with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_By-(1-s)x,d_Bx)$ in terms $B^{k-1}\oplus B^k$ Explicitly a degree-$k$ Hom element has components $(\alpha,\beta)$ on $S[1]$ and $S$; the identification is $(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto((-1)^{k-1}\alpha,\beta)$. Its differential becomes the displayed one by $d\alpha=d_B\alpha-(-1)^k u^*\beta$ and $d\beta=d_B\beta$.

source.place: Tag 0A0A, label lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals, proof; K-injective input Tag 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective); derived.tex Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective)

proof.text: Apply the strict-tower theorem to $H_\bullet$. More explicitly, the tower category is Grothendieck: colimits and filtered exactness are levelwise; if $G$ is a generator of $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, the direct sum of its images under the left adjoints to all evaluations is a generator, since evaluation detects nonzero morphisms. The ringed-site Grothendieck theorem supplies $G$, and the general degreewise-injective K-injective existence theorem therefore applies to this tower category. Take a K-injective tower resolution $H_\bullet\to J_\bullet$ with injective terms. Its evaluations $J_m$ are K-injective: evaluation has the exact left adjoint which places a module at levels $1,\ldots,m$, with identity transitions there and zero above $m$; adjunction carries maps from acyclic complexes to null-homotopic maps. Thus $H_m\to J_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives and is a homotopy equivalence: the comparison principle gives $g:J_m\to H_m$ with $g f\simeq 1$, and its injectivity with target $J_m$ gives $f g\simeq 1$. The termwise product map $\prod H_m\to\prod J_m$ is a homotopy equivalence (take the product of the component inverses and homotopies); it commutes with $1-s$. The induced map of mapping fibres is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. For an injective tower $J^k$, the monomorphism $L_m(F)\hookrightarrow L_{m+1}(F)$ of these evaluation left adjoints shows that $\operatorname{Hom}(F,J_{m+1}^k)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F,J_m^k)$ is surjective; taking $F=J_m^k$ splits each transition. Consequently $1-s:\prod J_m^k\to\prod J_m^k$ is surjective on sections: recursively choose $x_{m+1}$ lifting $x_m-y_m$, starting with $x_1=0$. Its kernel is $\lim J_m^k$. The resulting short exact sequence of complexes gives the canonical quasi-isomorphism $(0,\iota):\lim J_m\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$; its quotient cone is contractible, being the cone of the identity on $\prod J_m$. Thus the strict-tower Roos computation identifies $\lim_m J_m$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod J_m\to\prod J_m)[-1]$. Consequently the fibre in step 4 computes the total right derived inverse limit of the strict tower $H_\bullet$. This construction fixes the comparison by actual maps of complexes, rather than by a choice of a map between abstract triangles.

source.place: Tag 0941, label lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; ringed-module version recorded by the cited strict-tower theorem

proof.text: The complexes $Q_m$ are K-flat: filter the bounded complex by its finitely many stupid truncations; tensoring an acyclic complex with each successive quotient gives a finite direct sum of a shift of that acyclic complex, and the degreewise split short exact sequences then give acyclicity of the total tensor complex by finite induction. Therefore $\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes Q_m)\to\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes Q_m)$ is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism of strict towers. It is an isomorphism in the derived tower category, and $R\lim$ sends it to an isomorphism. Combining steps 3--5 with its inverse gives $\theta_N$. A quasi-isomorphism of representatives gives the same commuting diagram, by evaluation and the functorial resolution defining derived internal Hom, so $\theta_N$ descends naturally to $D(\mathcal O)$.

proof.text: The compatible projections $P_m\to\mathcal O[0]$ induce the augmentation $T\to C_b\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathcal O[0]$. Precomposition sends $x\in I$ to the family of Hom maps supported on $P_m^0$, all with value $x$; under evaluation these are exactly the degree-zero maps $I\to I\otimes Q_m$. Their family lies in $\ker(1-s)$, so the map into the fibre is $x\mapsto(0,(x)_m)$. Composing with $\lim J_m\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ is the same map obtained by factoring the compatible component maps $I\to J_m$ through $\lim J_m$. This proves the asserted equality with the strict-tower unit, including its naturality, before passing to the derived category.

proof.text: Restriction to $\mathcal C/U$ is exact, and $I|_U$ is K-injective by the cited restriction lemma. The Hom definition gives $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I)|_U=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L|_U,I|_U)$ by evaluating its sections over objects over $U$. Restriction preserves products (they are sectionwise), finite totalizations and the displayed cone. Hence the fibre in step 4 restricts to precisely the fibre constructed on the slice from $P_m|_U$ and $I|_U$. Steps 4--6 applied on that slice identify this fibre with the strict derived limit of the restricted tower. All evaluation, projection and $1-s$ maps are the same after further restriction, so both the comparison and the unit commute with those restrictions and with maps of $N$. No assertion that arbitrary products of sheaves are exact is used.

proof.text: For $r=0$, all $P_m$ and $Q_m$ are $\mathcal O[0]$, all transitions are identities, and $C_b=\mathcal O[0]$. In the fibre model the map $1-s:\prod I\to\prod I$ is split surjective as a map of complexes: solve $x_m-x_{m+1}=y_m$ by $x_1=0$ and $x_{m+1}=x_m-y_m$ (only finite sums for each component). Its kernel is the diagonal copy of $I$. The inclusion $I\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ from step 7 is therefore a quasi-isomorphism giving the constant-tower identification. Under it $\theta_N$ and the unit are the identity.
